newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast light crudes fall, few buyers seen.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast light crudes fall, few buyers seen.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes eased Wednesday, amid flat discounts and weaker sweet grades, traders said.

Alaska North Slope (ANS), the West Coast benchmark, fell five cents from Tuesday to $19.13/19.33 a barrel as weekly inventory reports showed a 6.4 million barrel build in nationwide crude supplies last week.
ANS, priced off national benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI), remained $1.02 under WTI, the price of a full cargo sold Monday by a key producer based in Houston.
Dominant ANS seller BP continued to offer ANS atr $0.90 cents under WTI, despite the cheaper sale.
"Would we move out (the discount) to do a deal....probably we would," said a BP trader.
No buyers spoke with BP, but traders heard bids as low as $1.10 off WTI, amid talk of ample Canadian and South American imports.
May trade for Line 63, another light grade, was expected to pick up later today following last week's lull for scheduling.

In California heavy markets, producers last week sold spot barrels of Wilmington crude at 0.85 and 0.79 cents a barrels, traders said. The grade has edged up ahead of springtime demand for road asphalt.

California Kern River crude eased Wednesday, tracking lower postings announced late Tuesday Chevron. Chevron, a main producer, lowered their posted price 50 cents, pressuring the Kern River's average price.
The grade has fallen over $4 since January and continues to come under pressure from WTI.
